detailed_descriptions.en: A cozy tidy up game where you have to organize potions to their respective shelves. Read the Encyclopedia and use your intuition to correctly fill every shelf! 100% Human made. No GenAI. Oh, no! Your potion sorting ritual backfired disastrously! Now all the 2979 potion bottles on the shelves of your master, the Grand Alchemist Joseph Grand’Oeur, are scattered all over the place. With your spells spent, you have to use your deductive skills, the shelf signage and the potions descriptions to tidy up the mess you made! 2900+ potions across 7 categories to sort through: From Healing to Poisons to Mischief , every potion has its place. Sorting them requires you to think like an alchemist. An Encyclopedia full of lore and clues, with 500+ unique entries, to help you complete each shelf: Discover the game’s rich story on your own terms, with every potion you pick up and examine. Two ways to play: 1. Puzzle - Narrative deduction as a sorting system: Use shelf signage that corresponds to each of the 7 potion categories, Encyclopaedia entries and a bit of intuition to help you sort the potions to their proper place. 2. Relaxed- Get in the flow and just sort All potions are discovered, their category unlocked. Experience the joy of sorting and looking at beautiful potion bottles. You can still open the book and read about the potions, but it's not required. No magical progression: Since magic is banned, there is no magical progression to unlock. But there might be some potions you can drink in the shop... Find them and ease your sorting experience! Or not, its your game! New rooms for you to unlock: Efficiency and exploration are key; place the correct potions in their proper place to unlock new areas. Special objects that can help you tidy up: Discover tools to help you reach high places, and carry more potions. A handcrafted, cozy atmosphere, inspired by apothecaries and alchemy shops: Watch the Alchemist’s shop return to order as you reorganize it, and immerse yourself in this cozy fantasy world.
